name: The Holm Oaks of Parque Bensaúde

location.address: Parque Bensaúde, Estrada da Luz, 1600 Lisboa

verified_sources: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (CC BY 4.0), processo AIP11063960I

https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parque_Bensa%C3%BAde
transport: About 15 minutes' walk from Colegio Militar/Luz station (Metro Blue Line)
verify_notes: Girth 3.12m, height 21m. One of two Italian/holm oaks (Quercus ilex) individually classified in Parque Bensauede, a former 17th century quinta (Quinta de Santo Antonio das Frechas) turned public park; the park separately holds the largest known cork oak in Lisbon, a different tree not in this register. A 2022-12-08 local news article (fregues.pt) independently confirms the park currently carries exactly four ICNF-classified trees of public interest: two Italian holm oaks, a red-flowering eucalyptus and a field maple, matching this register set exactly. Register age is age at 2017 measurement; 100 years then is roughly 109 now, stated loosely. Companion holm oak (lis_023) stands about 52m away in the same park.

name: The Paperbark of Jardim Constantino

location.address: Jardim Constantino, Rua Passos Manuel, 1150 Lisboa

verified_sources: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (CC BY 4.0), processo AIP11065641I
https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jardim_Constantino
transport: Short walk from Arroios or Anjos station (Metro Green Line)
verify_notes: Girth 1.58m, height 18m, crown 11m. Portuguese Wikipedia's Jardim Constantino article independently describes this exact tree as 'a Melaleuca styphelioides Smith, known as the paperbark tree, unique in Lisbon,' classified as of public interest in 1996. Jardim Constantino is a small (0.28 ha) public garden inaugurated 1889 in Arroios, named for florist Constantino Jose Marques de Sampaio e Melo, with a lake, playground and a Prometheus statue. Register age is at 2017 measurement (107), roughly 116 now. Its companion Moreton Bay fig (lis_027) grows a few metres away in the same small garden, so this reads as one short stop rather than two separate walks.

name: The Plane Tree of Hospital Pulido Valente

location.address: Hospital Pulido Valente, Alameda das Linhas de Torres 117, 1769-001 Lisboa

verified_sources: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (CC BY 4.0), processo KNJ1/064

the book 'Arvores da Cidade' (cited via press coverage), which independently gives the same tree as 364 years old, 30m tall with a 33m crown, standing in front of the Edificio D. Carlos and used as a venue for hospital anniversary events
access: Free, grounds of a public NHS hospital (Hospital Pulido Valente, part of ULS Santa Maria); the tree stands in the open forecourt of Edificio D. Carlos, visible without entering clinical areas, but visitors should behave as hospital guests
transport: Near Hospital Pulido Valente / Lumiar (Metro Yellow Line, short walk)
verify_notes: Girth 5.85m, height 28m, crown 37m. Register age 364 at 2015 measurement (so roughly 375 now) is corroborated almost exactly by an independent source, the book Arvores da Cidade, which separately gives 364 years and near-identical height/crown figures for what is unmistakably the same tree at the same hospital. This would make it easily the oldest documented plane tree in the Lisbon file and one of the oldest in the whole corpus, which is exactly the kind of outlier register age BRIEF_RESEARCH.md says to flag rather than quietly accept: two sources agree, but neither is a scientific dating, both trace back to the same municipal classification record from 1945. Classified since 1945, among the oldest classification dates in the Lisbon register. Flagging for the writer to state the age plainly as a register/book figure rather than a certainty. Access is genuine but institutional: it is a working public hospital, not a park, so the story should say so honestly.
